teams.name: Australia
teams.team_brief:
Having crashed out before the final in the last two World Cups, the most successful side in Women’s cricket history are under a little bit of pressure. However, they have the ingredients to win it all, even after Alyssa Healy’s retirement.

Australia’s top four - Georgia Voll, Beth Mooney, Phoebe Litchfield, and Ellyse Perry - is as power-packed as a batting core can get, while their bowling is the most varied in the tournament. Additionally, they have the best win-loss record against World Cup teams since the last edition; 10 wins and 2 losses.

star_player.name: Phoebe Litchfield
star_player.reasoning:
Phoebe Litchfield is a talented top order bat, who is exceptionally gifted at conventional as well as inventive strokeplay. She can seamlessly switch tempos, making her an excellent tactical weapon for Australia.

In the 2026 WPL, Litchfield smashed 243 runs in just 6 matches at a blazing strike rate of 154.78. Although a quad injury in late January abruptly ended her tournament and forced her into rehabilitation, she remains one of the most in-form batters at the tournament.

teams.name: England
teams.team_brief: England will enjoy the advantage of playing at home, with familiar conditions and passionate support expected to play a key role in their campaign. Led by Nat Sciver-Brunt, they boast a squad filled with match-winners and a blend of experience and youth that makes them one of the strongest sides in the tournament. Their recent form is encouraging, with back-to-back 2-1 T20I series wins over India and New Zealand.

star_player.name: Lauren Bell
star_player.reasoning: Lauren Bell has emerged as the leader of England's pace attack. The tall right-arm seamer generates steep bounce, swings the new ball effectively, and has become a genuine wicket-taking threat in all phases of a T20 innings. Bell heads into the World Cup in excellent form. She picked up 12 wickets in the WPL for Royal Challengers Bengaluru at an economy of just 5.53. In England’s warm-up series against India, she claimed 7 wickets in 3 matches at an average of 14.7 and an economy rate of 8.6.

teams.name: India
teams.team_brief:
India are coming into the World Cup uneasy. They will be riding the tailwind from last autumn's stirring ODI World Cup triumph, but since then, their T20 form has been patchy: a thumping 5-0 win against Sri Lanka, a 2-1 win in Australia, then a 1-4 loss in South Africa and a 1-2 loss in England last month. 

Here in England, they will be reliant on their strong batting order to weather the conditions and deliver big totals. Alongside the leadership duo of Harmanpreet Kaur & Smriti Mandhana, keep an eye out for Richa Ghosh, Jemimah Rodrigues, & Shafali Verma.

star_player.name: Smriti Mandhana
star_player.reasoning: Smriti Mandhana is a world-class left-handed opening batter and the vice-captain of the Indian team. India's batting unit is infamously top-heavy, and a lot of their hope rests on her shoulders. Luckily for India, the southpaw is in good nick. Mandhana led RCB to their second WPL title earlier this year, while also finishing as the tournament’s leading run-scorer with 377 runs at a strike rate of 153.25.

teams.name: West Indies
teams.team_brief: The 2016 Champions made their first semi-final in six years at the 2024 T20 World Cup, but their record since has been a mixed bag. Bilateral Series wins against Bangladesh and South Africa, along with the recent tri-series win against Ireland and Pakistan, have been encouraging - but a combined 1-10 record against England, Australia, India, and Sri Lanka cements their inconsistent reputation. That said, with multiple players from their title-winning squad still in the side, they can give anyone a game on their day.

star_player.name: Hayley Matthews
star_player.reasoning: Hayley Matthews is West Indies’ one truly elite player. As her country’s leading run-scorer and second-leading wicket-taker since the last World Cup, she is arguably the most valuable player in the competition. Of the West Indies’ last seven player of the series awards going back to July 2023, six have been won by Hayley Matthews. She comes into this tournament on the back of a victorious tri-series win in Ireland, where she scored 123 runs at an average of 61.5 and took 2 wickets.

teams.name: Netherlands
teams.team_brief: The Netherlands head into their maiden Women's T20 World Cup as one of the tournament's most exciting underdog stories. Having steadily climbed the ranks in recent years, they arrive in England with a clear identity, a close-knit squad, and the confidence that comes from earning their place through a hard-fought qualification campaign. They then fine-tuned their preparations in a tri-series in Scotland. The highlight was a historic 8-run win over Bangladesh, their first-ever T20I victory against the South Asian side.

star_player.name: Babette de Leede
star_player.reasoning: At just 26 years of age, Babette de Leede is already the heartbeat of Netherlands women's cricket. She’s a right-handed wicketkeeper-batter and captain of the side. Two years before the tournament, she made qualifying for the 2026 World Cup the team's stated goal, and drove the group towards it with relentless hard work. A captain who leads from the front in every sense.

teams.name: Scotland
teams.team_brief: Scotland are a well-balanced team playing their second consecutive World Cup. They enter on the back of a tri-series win against fellow World Cup nations Bangladesh and the Netherlands. Most recently, they beat Pakistan by 41 runs in a warm-up game. Scotland’s well-balanced squad is likely to be aided by the English conditions, with most of the squad featuring in various county setups across England.

star_player.name: Kathryn Bryce
star_player.reasoning: Kathryn Bryce’s ability to anchor and accelerate Scotland’s batting while also being a powerplay wicket-taker makes her their most valuable player. Part of a rare group of associate cricketers to have featured in women’s cricket’s three biggest franchise leagues, Scotland will need Bryce’s big-match experience and all-round skills to battle the big teams.

teams.name: Sri Lanka
teams.team_brief:
Sri Lanka’s win against South Africa in the opening game of the 2023 T20 World Cup marked the beginning of their rise as a competitive team at the highest level. Historic series wins in England and South Africa followed soon after, while the team won their first-ever Asia Cup on home soil in 2024. 

Sri Lanka have yet to make a knockout appearance at a T20 World Cup, but have been drawn in the relatively easier group. On the back of series wins in Bangladesh and the West Indies this year, The Lionnesses will go into this year’s tournament with high hopes.

star_player.name: Chamari Athapaththu
star_player.reasoning:
Chamari Athapaththu is one of the greats of women's cricket, and the heartbeat of this side. She has won all five of Sri Lanka’s player of the series awards since August 2023, which includes accolades for a historic series win in England and the country’s inaugural Asia Cup victory. 

Athapaththu comes into the World Cup as her team’s leading run-scorer in unbeaten series wins against West Indies and Bangladesh, while also picking up 6 wickets in those matches.

teams.name: South Africa
teams.team_brief: South Africa start as strong contenders for the World Cup. They boast a well-balanced squad featuring experienced campaigners, explosive batters, and a versatile bowling attack. Having reached the finals of the last two Women's T20 World Cups, the Proteas have established themselves as one of the most consistent teams in world cricket and will be eager to finally convert their recent success into a maiden ICC title.

star_player.name: Laura Wolvaardt
star_player.reasoning:
Laura Wolvaardt is one of the most elegant and technically accomplished batters in world cricket. The South African captain is known for her timing, composure under pressure, and ability to play in different gears. Equally adept against pace and spin, Wolvaardt is the cornerstone of South Africa's batting. 

She enters the World Cup in exceptional form. In South Africa's recent T20I series win over India, Wolvaardt amassed a record-breaking 330 runs in 5 matches at an average of 82.50 and a strike rate of 168.36, including a century and three half-centuries.

teams.name: Bangladesh
teams.team_brief:
Bangladesh were the surprise package of the 2025 ODI World Cup, beating Pakistan and pushing South Africa, Sri Lanka & England to the wire. The fearlessness of their young guns - with bat and ball - made them the neutral’s favourites last October. The Tigresses have not been in great form in their pre-World Cup games, but should hope that their thorough preparation on British soil will benefit them.

In the shorter, more equalising format of T20s, Bangladesh can reasonably hope to cause at least one upset in a tough group that features Australia, India & South Africa.

star_player.name: Marufa Akter
star_player.reasoning:
The Bangladeshi pacer burst on to the big stage at the ODI World Cup, with no less a luminary than Lasith Malinga praising her match-winning 2/31 against Pakistan. Marufa Akter ended the tournament with 6 wickets in 6 games, as her devastating swing kept wrong-footing opening batters. 

In English conditions, the 21-year old should cause havoc; she’s already picked up 5 wickets in the 6 pre-tournament games Bangladesh has played in the country.

teams.name: Pakistan
teams.team_brief:
Pakistan will be amongst the youngest and most exuberant teams at the World Cup, with five World Cup debutants. They haven't been a great tournament side so far, and their recent form is a bit patchy. In addition, confusion around whether Wahab Riaz is their head coach or just a mentor isn't conducive to the best preparatory conditions. 

They entered their World cup warm ups in peak confidence, after a 3-0 whitewash of Zimbabwe. However, they faced a sterner test in the subsequent tri-series in Dublin, failing to secure a single victory against Ireland and the West Indies.

star_player.name: Fatima Sana
star_player.reasoning: Fatima Sana is a superstar all-rounder and the talismanic captain of the Pakistan national team. At just 24, she is already ranked among the top ten all-rounders globally. Historically a bowling-heavy side, Pakistan often rely on Sana’s brutal ball-striking to inject late-innings acceleration. She enters the World Cup in scintillating T20 form, after a successful all-round series against South Africa, and on the back of scoring the fastest half-century in Women’s T20I history - 15 balls - against Zimbabwe.

teams.name: New Zealand
teams.team_brief:
This the end of a successful cycle for the defending champions, with icons Suzie Bates, Sophie Devine, and Lea Tahuhu set to retire after the World Cup. However, in all-rounder extraordinaire and new skipper Amelia Kerr, they have a capable leader leading as strong a unit as any in this tournament.

New Zealand have won twice the number of matches they've lost since the last World Cup, and dominated their recent home summer against Zimbabwe and South Africa. The 1-2 loss in England seems a mere blip.

star_player.name: Amelia Kerr
star_player.reasoning: Just days before the World Cup kicks off, Amelia Kerr reclaimed her spot as the ICC’s No. 1 ranked T20I all-rounder. Her recent form has been spectacular across franchise and international cricket. In the WPL 2026, she scored 210 runs and took 14 wickets in just 7 games. Then, she won Player of the Series against South Africa - including a maiden T20I. As the older legends fade around her, Kerr remains the linchpin of New Zealand's team balance.

teams.name: Ireland
teams.team_brief:
Ireland come into this World Cup in encouraging form, with wins over Bangladesh, Pakistan and West Indies in their pre-tournament games. However, despite that momentum and the luck of being in the easier group, Ireland will be lucky to get anything from most of their fixtures.

With a cohort of young talent showing potential - the Green & Whites have 9 players aged 24 or younger - this tournament may be a couple of years too early for them. However, the experience of playing at home will hopefully hold them in good stead.

star_player.name: Orla Prendergast
star_player.reasoning:
When the first WPL Mega Auction wrapped in late 2025, it was a shock that Orla Prendergast hadn’t found a team. In hindsight, it made sense; Ireland’s World Cup qualifiers clashed with the 2026 edition, and the all-rounder wouldn’t have been available anyway.

However, the fact that an Irish player’s snubbing was so surprising is an indication of the 24-year old’s prodigious talent. The latest display of her effectiveness came a couple of weeks ago, as she took 2/26 and scored 71* to single-handedly beat the West Indies. Ireland will need more of the same if they are to stand a chance of causing an upset at the World Cup.
